chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from some of his companions, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from his father, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a group of people who sent their hunting dogs, all of which were trained, and they had called out to them. When the dogs had gone, a strange dog entered among them, whom they did not know the owner of, so they all participated in the hunt. He said: 'It is not permissible to eat from it, because you do not know if it was caught by a trained dog or not.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on hunting prey when an unknown dog joins the pack?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) versus *shakk* (doubt) in hunting laws. He rules that the prey is *makhruj* (excluded from consumption) because the hunter cannot definitively prove that the specific trained dogs, upon whose name the slaughter was invoked, actually caught the prey, thereby creating uncertainty about the validity of the *tasmiyah*.
